title: An Optimized Immunoprecipitation Protocol for Assessing Protein-RNA Interactions In Vitro
protocol: Harvest cells for further processing.
Pellet cells by centrifugation in a swing-bucket rotor at 300 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Carefully discard supernatant.
Wash cell pellet once with PBS.
Resuspend the cells in 4 mL of ice-cold Lysis Buffer containing fresh protease inhibitors.
Mix by constant rocking for 30 min at 4°C.
Briefly spin down the samples at 4°C.
Sonicate the samples using 4 cycles of 5 s ON and 30 s OFF at 50% amplitude.
Mix the cell suspension well to make it homogeneous before sonication.
Place the 15-mL polystyrene tube in an ice-water bath during sonication to avoid protein degradation due to heating.
Use short ON pulses for sonication to minimize sample heating.
Avoid foaming during sonication to maintain efficiency.
Measure protein concentration with Bradford reagent using an appropriate standard.
Use 1 mg of whole cell protein extract for each immunoprecipitation in a Protein-LoBind Eppendorf tube.
Bring the reaction to 100 mM NaCl by adding Lysis Buffer without NaCl and adjust to a final volume of 1.5 mL with Lysis Buffer 100 mM NaCl.
Add 1 μg of antibody per mg of protein to the corresponding pre-labeled tube.
Include a mock IP, using the non-immune IgG fraction from the same species in which the antibody was made.
Add 100 U of Benzonase and MgCl2 to a final concentration of 1.5 mM to each tube to remove DNA and RNA molecules.
Allow immunocomplexes to form by rotating slowly at 15-30 rpm for 12-16 hours at 4°C.
Seal tube caps with parafilm to prevent leakage.
Incubate magnetic DynabeadsTM Protein G in a clean 1.5-mL tube using the desired volume of magnetic bead slurry (10 μL per 1 μg antibody).
Resuspend magnetic beads by rocking the vial; avoid vortexing.
Add 1 mL of 100 mM NaCl Lysis Buffer to the resuspended beads.
Rotate for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Place the tube on a DynaMag™-2 magnet, invert 3-4 times to facilitate adherence.
Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the magnetic beads.
Rotate magnetic beads in suspension for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Place the tube on a magnet; allow beads to adhere and supernatant to clear.
Remove the supernatant from the tube.
Process samples on ice to prevent degradation of protein and RNA.
Wash the beads by adding 1 ml of 100 mM NaCl Lysis Buffer with protease inhibitors.
Rotate the solution for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Place the tube on the DynaMag™-2 magnet.
Allow the beads to bind the magnet and the solution to become totally clear.
Remove the supernatant.
Wash beads with protein-RNA complexes.
Add 1 mL of RIP Buffer with protease inhibitors.
Rotate 5 min at 4°C.
Place the tube on the DynaMag™-2 magnet to separate beads from the solution.
Carefully remove the supernatant using a micropipette.
Repeat wash steps (a–d) five times.
Resuspend the complexes in 50 μL of RNase-free water.
Transfer the resuspended complexes to a new 1.5-mL tube.
Save 5 μL of the immunobound complexes to validate the immunoprecipitation by Western Blot.
Add 10 μL of Milli-Q water and 5 μL 4× Laemmli buffer to the saved complexes.
Boil the samples for 5 min at 95°C.
Store the boiled samples at −20°C until use.
Add 450 μL of TRIzol™ to the remaining 45 μL of beads containing the protein-RNA immunocomplexes.
Mix well by vortexing 15 s to allow elution of RNA from complexes.
Incubate the samples at 20°C–25°C for 5 min.
Add 0.2 mL of chloroform per mL of TRIzol™ reagent used in step 25.
Securely cap the tube and shake vigorously or vortex briefly.
Incubate 3 min at 20°C–25°C.
Centrifuge samples at 12,000 × g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Angle the tube at 45° and pipette the upper aqueous solution to a new RNase-free Eppendorf.
Avoid transferring any of the interphase or organic layer.
Add 0.5–1 μL of RNase-free glycogen (1 mg/mL stock).
Add 0.5 mL of isopropanol per mL of TRIzol™ reagent used in step 26.
Mix by inversion 10 times.
Incubate the samples for 10 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Centrifuge samples at 12,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Discard supernatant with a pipette.
Add 1 mL of pre-chilled ethanol 75% per mL of TRIzol™ reagent used in step 26.
Vortex briefly and centrifuge at 7,500 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully discard all supernatant with a micropipette.
Allow the pellet to air dry for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Resuspend in 20 μL of RNase-free water.
Quantify IPed RNAs using Qubit RNA HS Assay Kit following manufacturer's protocol.
Prepare a 1% agarose gel with filtered TAE 1×.
Clean the gel bed and combs with tissue wipes that do not leave fibers behind.
Treat half of the volume to be visualized in the gel with RNase A.
Incubate RNA (≤1 μg) with 25 U of RNase A for 20 min at 37°C.
Keep the treated samples on ice.
Load IPed samples (±RNase A) using an Orange G-based loading dye.
Run the gel for 15 min with 80 V.
Prepare a post-staining solution by adding 45 μL of ethidium bromide per 50 mL of filtered TAE.
Incubate the gel in the post-staining solution for 1 h at 20°C–25°C.
Prepare cDNA from the co-IPed RNA sample and quantify the specific transcript abundance by real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR).
Perform first strand cDNA synthesis from the IPed RNA obtained in step 27.
Mix 4 μL of 5× qScript cDNA SuperMix with the RNA (10 pg to 1 μg) and bring to 20 μL with RNase-free Milli-Q water.
Briefly vortex and spin down the samples.
Incubate at 25°C for 5 minutes.
Incubate at 42°C for 30 minutes.
Incubate at 85°C for 5 minutes.
Set up the RT-qPCR reaction.
Plan the RT-qPCR plate for determining the abundance of a target of interest among the IPed RNA.
Use triplicates for each sample and gene, including one negative control not bound by your protein of interest.
Dilute the cDNA 1/10–1/100 for RT-qPCR.
Prepare a mix for each primer pair containing SYBR™ Green and the primers as follows.
Mix thoroughly and centrifuge briefly to spin down the contents and eliminate any air bubbles.
Transfer 11 μl of the master mix to the corresponding well of the 96-well plate using an electronic pipette.
Add 4 μl of the diluted cDNA to the appropriate wells.
Seal the plate with an optical adhesive cover suitable for RT-qPCR detection.
Briefly centrifuge the plate to spin down contents and eliminate air bubbles.
Introduce the plate in the Thermocycler and set the appropriate program.
